questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I applied for multiple destinations and I got accepted at my first priority, which was really nice. I really wanted to learn the Levant dialect and that's why I chose Jordan, Amman for my study destination

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me since I got a lot of help in generel from family relatives and the university was also helping me. I faced no challenges which was really nice.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assistance with practical stuff as setting up my phone and downloading helpfull applications, and also doing my visa. I already knew a lot but it was really a blessing to receive help

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was some confusing about the exams dates which was a little bit upsetting since I already booked my flight home, but it was solved very quickly.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived closed to the campus, which was very easy to find. There is a lot of opportunities to find a good apartment/room close by

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's nice if you want to avoid morning traffic, but if you want more of a lively neighbourhood maybe you should find another area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I recommend not to book anything in advance. In the first week book a hotel and then go around the city to see which vibe each area gives you and then decide from there

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy to register and also very easy to get help if you need it

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I went to the center to register with my friends and there was a woman helping us through the process and what we needed to do. They informed us about the placement test and which dates were important to participate in different introduction procedures

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help both through mail and at the actual language center

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful and easy, I was registered at the classes through the placement test and I was very satisfied

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try your best at the placement test, and then afterwards you can try other levels if you are not satisfied

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the courses and academic programme since my level was in all arabic. Only my grammar teacher would speak a little bit of English if I didn't understand. It was another way of learning arabic and it was really beneficial since I was forced in another way of understanding and speaking the language

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was level 4

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very intense since it was all in arabic which was really nice, and I learned a lot of new vocabulary. Some of the things were the same, example reading texts and learning new vocabulary

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Grammar course
Dialect course 
Speaking course
Journalism and media course
Listening course
Writing course

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The courses was all apart of my semester abroad at the language center and they were all very beneficial

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think it's what you prioritise using your money on. You can live really cheap and buy groceries and order food for very cheap money. There are also more expensive solutions and opportunities if you want to, it depends on you what you want and also which area you go to

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can't really say so much about this topic since I didn't participate in any of it. There was a lot of really good cafe's and food opportunities at the host institution, and the language center also arranged a lot of nice trips to places in Amman and outside of Amman.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trips to a lot of nice places

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go out with your new friends. Its a nice way to get to know them in another way instead in the class room

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Seeing parts of the country or maybe visit a country nearby

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy for me. The people in Jordan are very friendly and helpfull

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do your homework together and participate in the trips. There is also very nice cafe's close to the university that you can visit after classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find anything challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way people respect each other and help each other

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask someone if you need help, be open to new friends and new learning ways and speak as much as you can even though you make mistakes

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe read about the grammar terms in arabic so you are ready for those classes. It would have helped me a lot in the start if I knew all the terms in arabic

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Understaning a lot more dialect and feeling good about the exams

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The grammar classes and speaking even though you are not sure in your words

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy the time you have because its going by really fast

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
